what: Per-run aggregates of the ADR 0003 measurement, 2026-11-13: Claude Code 2.1.322, claude-opus-5-5 at --effort high (the stack's lead model, claude-fable-5-2, was not measured), each run in a fresh detached worktree at main 9c5daaa (worktrees_and_sign_in). Assembled by hand from the raw runs, which stay private (paths, replies, transcripts), and from the measurement's notes; no builder script was written, so this file cannot be regenerated from the published scripts (its medians and totals can be recomputed from it). Grading notes are the measurement's; 'recheck' holds what a re-check of the raw runs and the owner's state found after the series, which replaces the measurement's notes where they differ. A with-run that broke containment is under failed_containment: counted as a failure and not re-run, which the pre-registration and the measurement's notes call void; void here means a run not counted (the stopped a1).

guard: before every always-on and R5 run: no listener on port 4002 (ss) and no process whose command line matches 'ibgateway' (pgrep -f); every run's exit code in the series logs is 0, so it never fired. pgrep -f matches whole command lines, and every run's own command line carried the deny rule Bash(*ibgateway*) (0003_common.sh lines 18 and 35), so these processes could trip other series' guards: ADR 0006 found its guard's match at 02:03:08 to be a process of this series. For a re-run, a re-run setup script (withdrawn) puts 0003_gateway_guard.sh in place of the as-run test (a test of process names and executables, never command lines, with a listener check on 7497 added; it cannot see a Gateway on the Windows side, reachable through mirrored networking) and moves the Bash(*ibgateway*) deny rule into a settings file, so no claude command line of a re-run carries that word
